summary: History of the U.S. Border Patrol from its racist 1924 founding through mass deportations, Operation Wetback, training Guatemalan death squads, and decades of killings, torture, sexual abuse and corruption up to 2020.

evidence.note: 1924 Immigration Act, built on eugenics, creates the Border Patrol
laws written for agribusiness but enforced by poor whites who hated Mexican workers
1929 unlawful-entry law and 1930s deportation of about a million, many US citizens
Harlon Carter, convicted of a 1931 killing, later Border Patrol chief and NRA head
Texas ranchers arm guards and fight Border Patrol raids to keep their migrant workforce
Operation Wetback launched June 1954 under General Swing, open-air camps in Los Angeles
agent John Longan sent to Guatemala in 1965 to build death squads, Operation Limpieza
Rios Montt era massacres of Maya villagers, the root of later Guatemalan migration
CIA bomb-making course for foreign police held at the Los Fresnos Border Patrol site
1980 reporting on rape, torture and using migrant children as bait to force confessions
post-9/11 dissolution of INS and creation of CBP in 2003
Trump era: BORTAC units deployed to police protests in US cities, up to 2020
